title: Natura 2000 Sites — Boundary Polygons and related lookup tables (EEA, version end 2024)
description:
Boundary polygons of all Natura 2000 sites across the EU, designated under the Birds Directive and the Habitats Directive, together with the related non-spatial lookup tables from the same EEA release. This collection is a GeoParquet re-encoding of the European Environment Agency's 'Natura 2000 (vector) — version end 2024' GeoPackage: the `NaturaSite_polygon` boundary layer plus the ten non-spatial tables that join to it on `SITECODE` (SPECIES, HABITATS, DESIGNATIONSTATUS, HABITATCLASS, BIOREGION, IMPACT, MANAGEMENT, OTHERSPECIES, METADATA, NATURA2000SITES) — all 11 GeoPackage layers, each exported to its own Parquet/GeoParquet file and independently accessible. The CRS of the spatial layer (EPSG:3035, ETRS89-extended / LAEA Europe) is unchanged from the source; no reprojection, simplification, or attribute transformation was applied.

The collection-level schema fields below (`table:columns`, `table:row_count`, `proj:epsg`, `geoparquet:*`) describe the primary `NaturaSite_polygon` layer specifically; the ten lookup tables have their own schemas, documented in the item's assets and in the README linked below.

Note also that per the source metadata, 19 Member States withhold species-site associations for sensitive species from the EEA database entirely — this is a limitation of the upstream data itself, not of this conversion.

Published as part of an exploration of cloud-native, FAIR distribution patterns for biodiversity spatial data (GeoParquet + STAC + machine-readable provenance), in the spirit of interoperable data space building blocks: persistent identifiers, explicit licensing, and recorded lineage that let both people and software agents establish trust in derived data without re-deriving it themselves. AI/Agent users: see AGENTS.md for field descriptions, query examples, and usage notes.

table:columns.name: SITECODE
table:columns.description: Persistent EU site identifier (e.g. 'NL3009017'), unique per Natura 2000 site. Join key to the non-spatial tables in the source GeoPackage (SPECIES, HABITATS, DESIGNATIONSTATUS, ...).

table:columns.name: SITENAME
table:columns.description: Official site name, generally in the national language of the designating Member State.

table:columns.name: MS
table:columns.description: Two-letter Member State abbreviation of the designating country (e.g. 'NL', 'AT').

table:columns.name: SITETYPE
table:columns.description: Designation-status code. A/D/F/H/J = Birds Directive (SPA) only; B/E/G/I/K = Habitats Directive (SCI/SAC) only; C = both directives overlapping. Source: EEA Natura2000 feature service field domain.

table:columns.name: INSPIRE_ID
table:columns.description: INSPIRE identifier URI for the site, where assigned by the Member State; frequently blank in this release.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Site boundary geometry in EPSG:3035 (ETRS89-extended / LAEA Europe), WKB-encoded.

processing:lineage: Downloaded 'Natura2000_end2024.gpkg' from the EEA SDI datastore (eea_v_3035_100_k_natura2000_p_2024_v01_r00). Read the 'NaturaSite_polygon' layer with geopandas.read_file(path, layer='NaturaSite_polygon') and wrote it directly to GeoParquet with GeoDataFrame.to_parquet() — no reprojection, filtering, or attribute changes. Verified against the source by: (1) asserting the parquet row count (27173) equals the feature count reported by pyogrio.read_info() for the same layer; (2) two independent site-level spot checks (SITECODE NL3009017 'Veluwe' and AT1101112 'Nickelsdorfer Haidel') confirming exact attribute equality and exact + topological geometry equality (bounds and area identical) between the source layer and the parquet output.
